**Pronúncia:** Ritmo e ênfase para nuances.
**24 palavras novas** (linguagem especializada).
**Texto do dia:** resenha / review.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo usar make em sentidos avançados (make do, make out, make up for, make for, make off with) numa resenha de um dicionário.

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Review: The Gilded Lexicon, 4th Edition
paras: This revised dictionary **makes up for** its steep price with sheer reach: 90,000 entries, each **made to earn** its place. Where earlier editions **made do with** a single example, the editors now give three, and they **make a point of** flagging register. Etymologies are succinct; some **make for** surprisingly gripping reading.

Not everything convinces. The typography is cramped, and I could barely **make out** the pronunciation key without a lens. A few definitions **make heavy weather of** simple words (the entry for “make” runs four pages). Still, it **makes good** on its promise: rarely has a reference book **made** such a **strong case** for itself.

items.q: Earlier editions gave three examples per entry.
items.why: made do with a single example.

items.q: The reviewer found the pronunciation key hard to read.
The reviewer considers the book a failure.

Sentido
Exemplo
rows: I could barely **make out** the key.

blocks.body: *Make* forma muitas **colocações** (*make a point of, make a case, make good on*). Em resenhas, serve para **avaliar**: *make for* + adjetivo + substantivo (*make for compelling reading*).
*Make for* (conduzir a) ≠ *make for* (dirigir-se a): *Make for the exit* = vá para a saída.

items.s: It ___ up for its price with sheer reach. (make)
Earlier editions ___ do with a single example. (make)
I could barely ___ out the pronunciation key. (make)

body: **Make a point of.** — Fazer questão de.
**Make good on.** — Cumprir, honrar.
**Make heavy weather of.** — Complicar demais.
**Make a case for.** — Argumentar a favor de.
**Make ends meet.** — Pagar as contas.
**Make light of.** — Minimizar.
**Make the most of.** — Aproveitar ao máximo.
**Make no bones about.** — Não ter rodeios sobre.
**Make waves.** — Causar polêmica.
**Make amends.** — Reparar o erro.
**Is the new edition worth the price?** — A nova edição vale o preço?
**Any complaints?** — Alguma queixa?
**It makes up for it with sheer reach.** — Compensa com a abrangência.

Exemplo

items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

prompts.model: His warmth makes up for his lack of experience.
We made do with cold sandwiches.
The memoir makes for compelling reading.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence review of a book, film or product using at least four different uses of make.
blocks.model: This guidebook makes up for its thin maps with vivid detail. The authors make a point of naming small cafés. Some chapters make for slow reading, but the history makes good company. I could barely make out the tiny index. Still, it makes a strong case for slow travel.
